questions.prompt: What JavaScript feature powers Vue 3's reactivity for objects?

options.text: Proxies (with get/set traps that track and trigger)

questions.explanation: Vue 3 uses Proxies: reads are tracked and writes trigger dependent effects to re-run. (Vue 2 used Object.defineProperty.)

options.text: Only reassignment of its .value, not deep mutations

questions.explanation: shallowRef reacts to .value being reassigned but not to deep mutations of the held object; use triggerRef to force an update after a deep change.

options.text: Creating a ref with custom control over when it tracks and triggers (e.g. a debounced ref)

questions.explanation: customRef gives you track and trigger functions so you decide exactly when the ref records a dependency and notifies effects — perfect for debounce/throttle.

questions.prompt: To flag an object so Vue never makes it reactive, wrap it with mark______. (complete the word)
questions.explanation: markRaw prevents an object from being converted into a reactive proxy — useful for third-party instances or large inert data.

questions.prompt: You deeply mutate a shallowRef's held object and the UI doesn't update. What's a correct fix?
questions.explanation: shallowRef only reacts to .value reassignment, so either reassign .value or call triggerRef to force dependent effects to re-run.

questions.prompt: Match each reactivity tool to its purpose.

pairs.right: Prevent an object from becoming reactive

questions.explanation: shallowRef limits depth, customRef customizes timing, toRaw unwraps a proxy, and markRaw opts an object out of reactivity entirely.
